questions.stem: According to traditional Chinese histories, the Shang dynasty was founded when Tang overthrew:
options: Qin Shi Huangdi, the first emperor
Di Xin, the last king of the Zhou
Jie, the last king of the Xia
King Wu, the founder of the Zhou
questions.explanation: Later texts say Tang of Shang defeated Jie, the wicked last ruler of the Xia. King Wu of Zhou overthrew the last Shang king, so he comes at the end of the dynasty, not the start.

questions.stem: A large walled city at Zhengzhou, with rammed-earth walls several kilometres long, is linked to the Erligang culture. Many archaeologists see it as:
options: a fortress built by the Qin to defend the northern frontier
a Neolithic village from long before the use of any bronze
an early Shang capital, from before the move to Anyang
the last capital of the Zhou kings after they moved east
questions.explanation: Zhengzhou is the major site of the Erligang phase, and many scholars identify it with an early Shang capital, though which named capital is debated. It belongs to the bronze-using Shang, centuries before the Qin.

questions.stem: Panlongcheng, a walled Erligang-style site near the Yangtze in Hubei, is important for understanding the Shang because it:
options: shows Shang influence reached far south, perhaps to secure copper
was the birthplace of the Shang royal family before they moved north
proves that the Shang directly governed all of modern China
contains the earliest oracle bones found anywhere in China
questions.explanation: Panlongcheng's Erligang-style bronzes and buildings show influence far from the Yellow River heartland, perhaps to control routes to metal ores. It does not prove direct rule over all of China, whose borders were far larger.

questions.stem: Historians debate the extent of the Shang state. Which interpretation best fits the evidence?
options: A loose league of equal cities with no king or central court of any kind
A small kingdom whose influence never reached beyond the walls of Anyang
A royal core near the Yellow River, with looser ties to allies and rivals beyond it
A unified empire with fixed borders and governors in every province of modern China
questions.explanation: Oracle bones show the king ruling a core region directly while dealing with allied, tributary and hostile groups around it, whose loyalty shifted. Provinces with governors belong to the later imperial system of the Qin and Han.

questions.stem: Before scholars recognised them in 1899, Shang oracle bones were dug up by farmers and sold as:
options: ornaments for the tombs of Qing dynasty officials
fuel for the kilns of local pottery workshops
'dragon bones' for use in traditional medicine
building material for the walls of Beijing
questions.explanation: Inscribed bones were ground up as 'dragon bones' in Chinese medicine until scholars noticed the ancient writing on them. Their source was later traced to the village of Xiaotun near Anyang.

questions.stem: The first scientific excavations at Anyang, from 1928 to 1937, were carried out by:
options: Japanese archaeologists working for the occupying army
the People's Republic of China after the 1949 revolution
the Academia Sinica's Institute of History and Philology
a British Museum team led by the explorer Aurel Stein
questions.explanation: Li Ji (Li Chi) led the Academia Sinica's excavations, with scholars such as Dong Zuobin and Liang Siyong, until the Japanese invasion halted work in 1937. The People's Republic resumed excavation after 1949.

questions.stem: The Anyang excavations are significant in the history of archaeology in China because they:
options: proved that the Xia dynasty had its capital at the site
helped introduce systematic, stratified excavation in China
were the first time any ancient Chinese site had been examined
recovered every royal tomb at the site untouched by robbers
questions.explanation: The team developed careful stratigraphic methods, recording layers and features, and trained a generation of Chinese archaeologists. Most of the royal tombs had been robbed in antiquity, and no writing links Anyang to the Xia.

questions.stem: The late Shang capital at Anyang is known to archaeologists as Yinxu, which means:
options: 'the Hall of Ancestors'
'the Ruins of Yin'
'the City of Heaven'
'the Northern Capital'
questions.explanation: Yin was the name for the late Shang capital, and Yinxu means the Ruins of Yin. The Zhou and later writers often called the Shang the Yin.

questions.stem: The royal cemetery at Xibeigang, near Anyang, contained huge cross-shaped tombs with sloping ramps. What did excavators find when they opened them?
options: They were empty cenotaphs, since Shang kings were cremated
They contained only oracle bones and no human remains at all
Most had been robbed in antiquity, but sacrificial pits survived
Each held its king's body untouched, with a full set of inscribed bronzes
questions.explanation: The great tombs had been looted long before, so much of their contents was lost, but rows of sacrificial pits with human and animal victims survived nearby. This is why the intact tomb of Fu Hao was so important.

questions.stem: Unlike the great royal tombs, the tomb of Fu Hao lay close to the palace and temple area at Xiaotun. Why does its discovery in 1976 matter so much?
options: It held the only Shang bronze vessels known to archaeologists
It proved that Fu Hao ruled as sole king after Wu Ding
It contained a written history of the Shang on silk scrolls
It was found intact, so its contents could be recorded in place
questions.explanation: Excavated by a team under Zheng Zhenxiang, it is the only undisturbed royal-family tomb from Anyang, so objects could be studied in context. Many Shang bronzes were already known from other sites.

questions.stem: Fu Hao's tomb contained jades from much older Neolithic cultures alongside Shang objects. What is the most reasonable inference?
options: Shang jade carvers copied foreign styles that they had never seen
The Shang elite collected or inherited older precious objects
Fu Hao herself lived during the Neolithic period
The tomb was reused by several different cultures over time
questions.explanation: Some jades in the tomb are in the styles of earlier cultures such as Hongshan and Liangzhu, suggesting they were heirlooms or collected treasures. Fu Hao is firmly dated to the reign of Wu Ding by inscriptions.

questions.stem: Fu Hao's tomb held bronze weapons, including large axes inscribed with her name. Together with oracle bones about her campaigns, these suggest that she:
options: was a captured enemy queen whose weapons were trophies
commanded armies in war on behalf of the king
was a weapon-smith who ran the royal bronze foundry
was buried with weapons only as a sign of her father's rank
questions.explanation: Oracle bones record Wu Ding divining about Fu Hao leading troops against enemies, and the inscribed axes were symbols of military authority. Together the written and archaeological evidence support her military role.

questions.stem: About sixteen human sacrificial victims and six dogs were buried in Fu Hao's tomb. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Human sacrifice was used only for women, never for kings
High-status Shang burials included sacrifices to serve the dead
Fu Hao was executed and buried with her guards as a punishment
The victims died of disease and were buried with her by chance
questions.explanation: Sacrificed people and dogs appear in many elite Shang burials, including royal tombs, reflecting beliefs about the afterlife and status. The pattern is not limited to women.

questions.stem: A full oracle bone inscription often has four parts. Which sequence is correct?
options: Question, answer from the ancestors, payment, royal seal
Title, king's name, list of enemies, oath of the army
Preface (date and diviner), charge, prognostication, verification
Prayer, sacrifice, cracking, then burial of the bone in the royal tomb
questions.explanation: Inscriptions give the day and diviner, the charge or topic, the king's reading of the cracks and sometimes a later note of what happened. The verification sections let historians check events against predictions.

questions.stem: Scholars group oracle bones into periods by the names of diviners and royal ancestors they mention. Most surviving inscriptions come from the reign of Wu Ding. What problem does this create?
options: Wu Ding's inscriptions are in a script no one can read
Our picture of the Shang is weighted heavily towards one reign
We cannot tell which inscriptions are Shang and which are Zhou
No oracle bones can be dated to any particular king
questions.explanation: Because Wu Ding's diviners produced such a large share of the inscriptions, generalisations about the Shang often rest on his reign. Later reigns have fewer and more routine inscriptions.

questions.stem: In 1917 the scholar Wang Guowei compared the names of royal ancestors on oracle bones with the Shang king list in Sima Qian's Shiji. What did he find?
options: The bones showed the Shang had queens rather than kings
The bones largely confirmed the king list written a millennium later
The bones proved the king list was invented by Han dynasty officials
The bones named only Zhou kings, so the Shang were legendary
questions.explanation: Wang Guowei showed that most royal names and their order in the Shiji matched the oracle bones, with small differences. This strengthened confidence in Sima Qian's account of the Shang, written in the Han period.

questions.stem: Shang oracle bones show that the person who most often interpreted the cracks and made the final prediction was:
options: the queen mother
the king
a village elder
the chief bronze-caster
questions.explanation: Diviners prepared the bones and recorded the questions, but the king usually gave the prognostication. This shows his role as the chief link between the living and the ancestors.

questions.stem: Shang kings were given posthumous temple names such as Wu Ding, Zu Jia and Di Xin. The second part of each name refers to:
options: one of the ten 'heavenly stems', which set the day of his sacrifices
the province in which the king had been born before taking the throne
the number of years the king had ruled before his death
the name of the Zhou ancestor who adopted the king as heir
questions.explanation: Each royal ancestor was linked to one of the ten heavenly stems, and offerings to him were made on the day of the ten-day week with that stem. This shaped a regular schedule of ancestor rites.

questions.stem: Oracle bones show that the throne often passed from a king to his younger brother before passing to the next generation. This tells us that Shang succession:
options: always passed from father to eldest son without exception
passed through the female line to the king's sister's son
could follow brothers as well as sons, within the royal lineage
was decided by an election held among the leading nobles each time
questions.explanation: The king list shows many brother-to-brother successions as well as father-to-son ones, especially in the earlier part of the dynasty. Succession stayed within the royal clan.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the Shang army?
options: The army was made up only of foreign mercenaries hired from the steppe
Nobles led levies with dagger-axes and bows, and chariots for the elite
A large standing army of paid professionals was armed entirely with iron swords
Cavalry archers on horseback formed the main fighting force of the state
questions.explanation: Shang forces were raised for campaigns and fought with bronze dagger-axes (ge), spears and composite bows, while chariots were a late, elite addition. Iron weapons and mounted cavalry came centuries later.

questions.stem: Oracle bones ask whether Fu Hao's childbirth would be 'good', and record that a daughter was judged 'not good'. What does this reveal about the status of women?
options: Childbirth was never a concern of the royal court
Sons were valued more, since the lineage passed through males
Women were forbidden to appear in any royal divination
Daughters inherited the throne, so sons were less desired at court
questions.explanation: The preference for a son shows the importance of the male line for succession and ancestor worship. Yet women such as Fu Hao could hold great power, so status depended on rank as well as gender.

questions.stem: Wu Ding is one of the best-known Shang kings because:
options: he was the founder who overthrew the Xia dynasty
he moved the royal capital from Anyang to the Yangtze River
he was the last Shang king, defeated by the Zhou
more oracle bones survive from his reign than from any other
questions.explanation: Wu Ding ruled at Anyang in the late Shang period, and his diviners produced a large share of all known oracle bones, recording campaigns, harvests, illness and his consorts. Tang founded the dynasty and Di Xin was its last king.

questions.stem: Shang writing on oracle bones is significant because it:
options: is a direct ancestor of the Chinese characters still used today
was an alphabet borrowed from traders in Mesopotamia
could be read only by priests and died out with the Shang
used pictures that stood only for whole sentences, not words
questions.explanation: Oracle bone script is a developed logographic system whose characters evolved into later Chinese writing. Only part of it has been deciphered, but it is not alphabetic and did not die out.

questions.stem: Very few Shang written records survive other than inscriptions on bone and bronze, but the character later used for 'book' shows bound strips. What does this suggest?
options: The Shang banned writing on any material except bone
Writing was invented only at the very end of the Shang
Bone and bronze were the only materials available in China
The Shang may also have written on bamboo, which has decayed
questions.explanation: The character ce appears to show slips tied together, and an early Zhou text says the Shang ancestors had records. Perishable bamboo and wood would not survive, so the surviving record is biased towards ritual inscriptions.

questions.stem: The Shang calendar combined ten 'heavenly stems' with twelve 'earthly branches' to name the days. How long was the full cycle?
options: 22 days
120 days
360 days
60 days
questions.explanation: Pairing ten stems with twelve branches in order gives 60 combinations before the cycle repeats, since 60 is the lowest common multiple of 10 and 12. The ten-day week, the xun, was also based on the stems.

questions.stem: Diviners regularly asked whether there would be 'no disaster' in the coming xun. A xun was:
options: a lunar month
a season of three months
a year of twelve months
a ten-day week
questions.explanation: The Shang counted time in ten-day weeks named after the ten heavenly stems, and divined at the end of each about the next. Months were lunar, with an extra month added when needed.

questions.stem: Many Shang bronze vessels are decorated with the taotie, which is:
options: a scene of farmers at harvest
a symmetrical, mask-like animal face
a lifelike portrait of the reigning king
a map of the Shang royal lands
questions.explanation: The taotie is a stylised face with eyes and horns, formed from two animal profiles facing each other. Its meaning is debated, but it is the most typical Shang bronze motif.

questions.stem: Oracle bones address the high god Di mostly through offerings to royal ancestors. Which statement best explains this pattern of worship?
options: The Shang believed Di could be reached only through animal spirits
Ancestors were feared as enemies of Di who caused all disasters
Ancestors were thought able to intercede with Di and affect the living
Di was a dead king whose tomb lay in the royal cemetery
questions.explanation: The Shang believed dead kings could intercede with Di and could also cause harm if not given offerings, so the king fed them through regular sacrifices. Di was a remote supreme power, not a deified king.

questions.stem: Oracle bones record sacrifices of people from the Qiang, a group often at war with the Shang. This suggests that many victims of human sacrifice were:
options: volunteers from noble families
criminals sentenced by a law court
priests who had made false predictions
prisoners taken in war
questions.explanation: Inscriptions often mention numbers of Qiang offered to ancestors, and skeletal studies at Anyang suggest many victims came from outside the local population. Warfare supplied captives for ritual killing.

questions.stem: The Shang dynasty ended when the Zhou defeated the last Shang king, Di Xin, at the battle of:
options: Kadesh
Muye
Changping
Red Cliffs
questions.explanation: King Wu of Zhou defeated Di Xin at Muye, usually dated to 1046 BCE, and Di Xin died soon after. Changping and Red Cliffs were much later Chinese battles, and Kadesh was fought between Egypt and the Hittites.

questions.stem: Sima Qian describes Di Xin as a cruel tyrant who wasted wealth on feasts and ignored good advice. Why should historians be cautious about this picture?
options: It was invented by twentieth-century archaeologists at Anyang
It draws on Zhou traditions that blamed the last king for the conquest
It was written by Di Xin's own son, who had wanted to inherit his throne
It is based on oracle bones that describe Di Xin's feasts in detail
questions.explanation: The Zhou justified their victory by saying Heaven had rejected a wicked Shang ruler, and later writers repeated a stock 'bad last king' story. Oracle bones of the late Shang show a king still campaigning and performing rites.

questions.stem: Late oracle bones record long Shang campaigns against peoples in the east. Which explanation of the Shang fall do many modern historians draw from this?
options: The Shang abandoned bronze, so their weapons were useless against iron
Foreign invaders from India conquered the Shang and the Zhou together
Costly wars weakened the Shang as the Zhou grew stronger in the west
A great flood of the Yangtze destroyed Anyang in a single year
questions.explanation: Historians link the fall to overextension against eastern peoples, defections of allies and the rise of the Zhou in the Wei River valley. Iron weapons were not yet in use, and Anyang is far from the Yangtze.

questions.stem: Before the oracle bones were found, some scholars doubted that the Shang had existed at all. Why?
options: Knowledge of the Shang came only from texts written centuries later
No Chinese writer had ever mentioned a dynasty called the Shang
The Zhou had ordered every Shang city to be renamed and forgotten
Western archaeologists had already shown Anyang to be a Han city
questions.explanation: Accounts such as the Shiji were written about a thousand years after the Shang, so sceptics in the early twentieth century questioned them. The discovery of Anyang turned the Shang into an archaeologically proven dynasty.
